title: Wavelength-resolved small-angle neutron spectroscopy of spin waves in MnSi under pressure
authors: E. V. Altynbaev, D. O. Skanchenko, Z. Xie, Y. Ke, Y. Bao, A. V. Tsvyashchenko
abstract: We report wavelength-resolved spin-wave small-angle neutron scattering (SWSANS) on the time-of-flight SANS instrument BL01 at the China Spallation Neutron Source and extend the method to pressure-cell measurements of MnSi. MnSi is used as a benchmark B20 helimagnet because its helimagnetic order and spin-wave stiffness are well characterized at ambient pressure. In a fixed magnetic field, the time-of-flight measurement provides a spectrum of neutron wavelengths. For each detector branch $s=\pm1$, the intensity profile is recentered relative to the wavelength-dependent Bragg angle $θ_B (λ) = k_s λ/ 2π$, and the cutoff angle $θ_C (λ)$ is extracted in the local branch coordinate. The cutoff-derived spin-wave stiffness $A$ is obtained from a linear fit of $θ_C^2$ as a function of $λ^2$. Ambient-pressure measurements reproduce the known stiffness scale of MnSi. Structural SANS at ambient pressure and at nominal 5 and 11 kbar verifies the magnetic state and provides an internal pressure-state check for the pressure-cell measurements. At nominal 11 kbar, within the present cutoff model, the cutoff-derived stiffness is substantially reduced, whereas the structural field scale $H_{C2}$ remains high. This contrast shows that $A$ cannot be inferred from static structural parameters alone under pressure. To our knowledge, these measurements constitute the first SWSANS implementation on a pulsed neutron source and the first SWSANS determination of spin-wave stiffness under pressure. The experiment also shows that reliable high-pressure SWSANS on a pulsed source requires high source brilliance, stable wavelength-dependent normalization, and sufficient statistics in each wavelength window.
summary: This work pioneers the use of wavelength-resolved small-angle neutron scattering ($	ext{SWSANS}$) to measure spin-wave stiffness ($A$) in $	ext{MnSi}$ under high pressure. By comparing dynamically measured $A$ values with structural predictions, the authors demonstrate a significant discrepancy at 11 kbar. This highlights that simple extrapolations from static magnetic parameters are insufficient for accurately characterizing quantum material properties under extreme conditions.
main_problem: The study aims to determine how spin-wave stiffness ($A$) in $	ext{MnSi}$ changes under hydrostatic pressure, specifically testing the reliability of structural parameters versus direct dynamic measurements.
main_result: At high pressure (11 kbar), the directly measured spin-wave stiffness ($A$) is substantially reduced compared to ambient pressure, demonstrating that $A$ cannot be reliably inferred solely from static structural magnetic parameters like the critical field ($H_{C2}$).
method: Wavelength-resolved small-angle neutron scattering ($	ext{SWSANS}$) was employed using a time-of-flight instrument on a pulsed source to measure spin-wave dynamics across a range of wavelengths.
model_or_system: The system is $	ext{MnSi}$, a benchmark B20 helimagnet exhibiting chiral magnetic order. The analysis relies on fitting the cutoff angle ($	heta_C$) derived from the intensity profile's edge position to extract the spin-wave stiffness $A$ via the relation $	heta_C^2 \propto \lambda^2$.
key_observables: Cutoff angle ($	heta_C$), spin-wave stiffness ($A$), structural critical field ($H_{C2}$), and transition temperature ($T_C$).
important_parameters: Ambient pressure values validate the method; at 11 kbar, $A$ is significantly reduced compared to ambient measurements.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes a local linear dispersion relation for spin waves ($\varepsilon(q) \propto A q^2$) and that the measured $	heta_C(\lambda)$ follows a predictable quadratic dependence on wavelength squared ($	heta_C^2 = a + b\lambda^2$).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the principle of wavelength-resolved SANS, show structural verification of magnetic fields ($H_{C2}$) at various pressures, and present linear fits comparing ambient vs. high-pressure measurements.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the methodology by adapting fixed-wavelength SANS to a time-of-flight, wavelength-resolved geometry. It validates this method using ambient pressure data before applying it to measure spin dynamics at 5 kbar and 11 kbar, culminating in a comparison between dynamic ($A$) and static ($	ext{H}_{C2}$) measurements.
why_interesting: While focused on magnetism, the technique itself—using advanced neutron scattering kinematics (wavelength-resolved measurement) to probe collective excitations under extreme conditions—is highly relevant for understanding many-body dynamics in strongly correlated quantum materials.

FIG. 2. Structural verification of the magnetic field scale for the ambient-pressure, nominal 5 kbar, and nominal 11 kbar powder datasets. Filled symbols show HC2(T), extracted from the disappearance of the elastic Bragg intensity, and open symbols show HC1m(T), defined as the field of maximum along-field Bragg intensity. Smooth monotonic root-like curves are guides to the eye constrained to vanish at the corresponding TC; they are not independent fits to the magnetic equation of state. Open markers at the baseline indicate TC anchors from zero-field temperature scans. Hatched colored boxes mark A-phase-like regions used as structural consistency checks.

FIG. 3. Representative cutoff-edge fits used in the wavelength-resolved SWSANS analysis. (a,b) Ambient-pressure MnSi: a 15 K, 8 kG left/beam-side example from PC4 (λ = 3.25 ˚A), and a 25 K, 7 kG right/outer-edge example from PC9 (λ = 5.75 ˚A). (c,d) Nominal 11 kbar MnSi at 4 K and 9 kG: right/outer-edge examples from PC8 (λ = 5.25 ˚A) and PC9 (λ = 5.75 ˚A). Symbols show locally averaged display points used only for readability, green curves show representative phenomenological arctan-step fits, and dashed vertical lines mark the accepted edge positions in the instrument q coordinate before conversion to θC.

FIG. 4. Linear θ2 C(λ2) plots. (a) Ambient-pressure MnSi at 15 and 25 K. (b) Nominal 11 kbar MnSi at 4 K, 9 kG; 8 K, 8 kG; and 10 K, 9 kG. Symbols show θ2 C values and dashed lines show linear fits; the 8 K, 8 kG fit is extended to its θ2 C = 0 crossing.

FIG. 5. Temperature dependence of the cutoff-derived spin- wave stiffness A. Filled symbols show the present wavelength- resolved SWSANS results at ambient pressure and at nominal 11 kbar. Open gray symbols and the dashed gray guide show the ambient-pressure reference scale from Ref. [11].
